what_it_does: Transformer models (the architecture behind ChatGPT and similar AI) consist of many repeated layers, each combining large matrix multiplications (multiplying two giant grids of numbers together), a normalization step, and an attention mechanism (which lets each word look at every other word). Previous chip designs tried to speed up individual pieces of these layers in isolation, but as models grew deeper and processed longer text, the cost of moving data between layers — shuffling numbers in and out of memory between each step — became the dominant bottleneck. TransFusion treats the entire stack of layers as one unified computation graph and pipelines it: while one layer's results are being computed, the next layer's inputs are already being loaded, and the memory layout of intermediate results is arranged to maximize reuse without spilling to slower memory. An algorithm called TileSeek (using a tree-search strategy similar to how game-playing AI explores moves) finds the best way to break computations into chunks that fit on-chip memory.
